learn.title: Solar Panel Types: Mono, Poly, Thin-Film
learn.intro: Solar panels are the backbone of renewable energy. Understanding their differences helps homeowners and businesses choose the best technology for their needs, accelerating the shift to clean energy.
learn.c1_text: Monocrystalline panels use single-crystal silicon, offering up to 22% efficiency. They’re ideal for limited spaces, like rooftops in cities where every square inch counts.
learn.c2_text: Made from melted silicon fragments, polycrystalline panels are 15-17% efficient and 10-20% cheaper. They’re popular in rural India for large-scale solar farms.
learn.c3_text: Thin-film panels are lightweight and flexible, with 10-13% efficiency. They’re used in India’s desert solar parks for their adaptability to harsh conditions.

learn.title: Solid-State Batteries: Safety & Energy
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with solid materials, reducing fire risks and storing more energy. This innovation is key for electric vehicles and grid storage.
learn.stat1: Solid-state batteries: 500+ Wh/kg vs. 250 Wh/kg for lithium-ion
learn.stat2: Lithium-ion fire rate: 1 in 10 million vehicles
learn.stat3: India’s EV market: 15% CAGR expected by 2030
learn.stat4: Solid-state batteries could cut EV costs by 30%

learn.title: How EVs Work: Motors & Charging
learn.intro: Electric vehicles use motors to convert electricity into motion. Regenerative braking and efficient charging systems make them a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel cars.
learn.c1_text: EVs use AC or DC motors to power wheels. A Tesla Model 3’s motor delivers 345 hp, outperforming many gasoline cars.
learn.c2_text: Regenerative braking recovers 70-80% of energy during deceleration, extending range by 10-15% in city driving.
learn.c3_text: India has 20,000+ public EV charging stations (2024), with plans to add 50,000 by 2025 to support 10 million EVs on roads.
learn.stat1: EV motor efficiency: 85-90% vs. 20-30% for internal combustion

learn.title: Solar PV & the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using the photoelectric effect. This process powers homes and drives the global energy transition.
learn.c1_text: Sunlight hits solar cells, knocking electrons loose. A single photon can generate 1 electron, powering devices like calculators.
learn.c2_text: Silicon layers create a p-n junction. When photons hit, electrons flow, creating direct current (DC) electricity.
learn.c3_text: India has 70+ GW of solar capacity (2024), with the world’s largest solar park in Gujarat. Policies like the National Solar Mission drive this growth.

learn.title: Lithium-Ion Batteries: Grid Storage
learn.intro: Lithium-ion batteries store energy for grids, enabling renewable energy use during peak demand. Their scalability is critical for energy security.
learn.c1_text: Lithium ions move between electrodes during charging/discharging. A 10 kWh battery can power a home for 10 hours.
learn.c2_text: Grid storage uses containers with 100+ kWh. India’s largest is 100 MW/200 MWh in Rajasthan, supporting solar farms.
learn.c3_text: India plans 15 GW of battery storage by 2025. Projects like the 100 MW/200 MWh in Rajasthan show its growing role in renewable integration.
learn.stat2: India’s grid storage target: 15 GW by 2025

learn.title: Sodium-Ion Batteries: Affordable Alternative
learn.intro: Sodium-ion batteries use abundant sodium, reducing costs and environmental impact. They’re a promising alternative for large-scale storage.
learn.c1_text: Sodium is 10x more abundant than lithium. Sodium-ion batteries cost 30-50% less, with energy density of 100-150 Wh/kg.
learn.c2_text: They operate at lower voltages, reducing thermal risks. Sodium’s atomic size allows faster ion movement, improving charge cycles.
learn.c3_text: India’s IRENA report highlights sodium-ion as a cost-effective solution. Projects in Gujarat aim to deploy 500 MWh by 2025.
